SAIL: Higher P/E Assumptions Will Struggle If Profit Margins Disappoint
news.body: Analysts have raised their fair value estimate for Steel Authority of India to ₹125 from ₹105, reflecting updated assumptions that include higher projected revenue growth, a slightly lower discount rate and a higher future P/E multiple, partially offset by a more cautious view on profit margins. Analyst Commentary For Steel Authority of India, the recent fair value increase to ₹125 reflects a more optimistic set of assumptions from analysts, particularly around revenue potential, the discount rate and the P/E multiple applied to future earnings.

news.body: Steel Authority of India Limited announced that the Government of India, Ministry of Steel, vide letter dated February 16, 2026, has redesignated the post of Director (Technical, Projects and Raw Materials) as Director (Mining). Accordingly, Shri Manish Raj Gupta has been redesignated as Director (Mining), Steel Authority of India Limited with effect from February 18, 2026. Shri Manish Raj Gupta, an accomplished professional with over three decades of experience in the steel industry, currently serves as Executive Director In-charge (Operations) at Steel Authority of India Limited. news.title: Third quarter 2026 earnings: Revenues exceed analysts expectations while EPS lags behind
news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: EPS: ₹0.91 (up from ₹0.34 in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹275.5b (up 13% from 3Q 2025). Net income: ₹3.74b (up 164% from 3Q 2025). Profit margin: 1.4% (up from 0.6% in 3Q 2025). The increase in margin was driven by higher revenue. Revenue exceeded analyst estimates by 3.7%. Earnings per share (EPS) missed analyst estimates by 9.0%. Revenue is forecast to grow 4.3% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 12% growth forecast for the Metals and Mining industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has fallen by 1% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 21% per year, which means it is well ahead of earnings.
